root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before the copied named-argument bytes can later be serialized as a `const char*` and compared with C-string semantics, `argnamebuffer` must reserve at least one byte beyond `argsize` for an in-bounds terminator.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original allocates exactly `argsize` bytes for `argnamebuffer` and copies `argsize` attacker-controlled bytes into it, so the later C-string conversion path has no spare terminator slot. The fixed original allocates `argsize + 1` bytes at the same source site, satisfying the missing capacity obligation before the name enters fmt's named-argument pipeline.

nodes.state: At the named-lookup compare, fmt uses `named_args.data[i].name == name`, so the raw pointer stored in the named-argument table is consumed at the exact callsite that immediately triggers the implicit `basic_string_view(const Char*)` / `strlen` path reported by AddressSanitizer.

When fmt serializes named arguments, `init_named_args()` stores only `arg.name.data()` in `named_arg_info.name`, leaving the lookup table with a raw `const char*` that no longer carries the original string-view length.

The `named_arg` object created by `fmt::arg(argname, item1)` still aliases the same attacker-controlled name buffer that `argnamebuffer` owns, so the later table serialization starts from that original storage.

edges.relation: The raw pointer written into `named_arg_info.name` at table-serialization time is later read back unchanged as `named_args.data[i].name` at the named-lookup compare.

The same name buffer alias held in `named_arg_base<Char>::name` is serialized into `named_arg_info.name`, which is the source-level step that drops the explicit string-view length and leaves only a raw pointer.
The pointer produced from `argnamebuffer.data()` at the fuzzer callsite is preserved as the `name` member of the `named_arg` object created by `fmt::arg(argname, item1)`.
